title: Bound
subtitle: A dancer inside a memory

body: Bound is Plastic's PlayStation 4 platform game, released on 16 August 2016. A princess moves through a shifting geometric world while the surrounding story follows a woman revisiting her childhood memories. The princess's movement draws on ballet, making each step, jump and defensive action part of a continuous performance. Abstract structures replace familiar landscapes, breaking apart and reforming as the journey continues. The personal events behind them are gradually revealed, giving the unusual scenery a connection to a life beyond the visible fantasy.

The dancer runs, balances and crosses gaps with gestures that retain the character of a performed routine. Dancing can repel threats, so an action used for protection also reinforces the way she occupies the space. Edge protection on certain platforms reduces accidental falls, allowing more attention to remain on the figure and changing environment. Some sections still carry a risk of falling, with a nearby return keeping the journey moving. The design gives the performance room to be watched rather than requiring every step to become a demanding platform challenge.

Scenes outside the princess's world connect its Queen, monster and collapsing structures to the woman's past. The player can recognise those relationships as the journey unfolds, reading the fantasy through the memories that surround it. Oleg Shpudeiko's music accompanies the movement and changing architecture. Critics praised Bound's visual identity and originality, while some found the interactions too limited. That balance defines the experience: its route is built to reveal a personal story through the dancer's body, the forms around her and the spaces that gradually disappear.
